Quick heads-up: were adding a telemetry vendor, TelemetryOps, to our subprocessor list to support performance monitoring for the Redwood Hosted API. Per our DPA, this triggers a 30-day notice and objection window.

What Im sending attached:
- subprocessor_list_20270627.csv (current list with TelemetryOps row highlighted)
- telemetryops-addendum-draft.pdf (proposed addendum to extend DPA scope to include TelemetryOps)

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm you received this notice and whether youll raise any objections within 30 days (window starts today, 2027-06-27).
2) If no objection, please sign the addendum via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/telemetryops-addendum/ACME-3742
3) If you need more technical detail (data residency, encryption, subprocessorsscope), loop in to this thread and well provide materials (SOC2, SCCs).

Were trying to keep this lightweight — happy to schedule a 30-minute sync if you prefer.

Best,
Olga Petrov

- Can you confirm TelemetryOps is subject to the same contractual protections (SCCs + DPA addendum) and technical controls (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, restricted key access)?
- If we have to object, what is the exact process and timeline? Wed like to understand escalation and remediation options.

Were reviewing internally; Ill aim to get a response by mid-week but wanted the clarifying questions on record.

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: proposed third-party addition (TelemetryOps) + objection window and e-sign

Hi Alex (and team),

Thanks for the questions — appreciate the thoroughness. Quick answers and next steps below:

1) Data residency: TelemetryOps will process telemetry and operational metadata generated by API calls. For Acme customers with EU region settings, telemetry will remain in EU buckets; TelemetryOps supports EU-only deployments and we will tag any EU tenant data to remain in EU at rest. For the initial deployment with Acme (per your account config) we do not plan to send EU tenant data to US.

2) Contractual & technical controls: TelemetryOps is being added as a subprocessor under Redwoods DPA. The addendum includes explicit incorporation of SCCs for EU transfers where applicable. Technical controls: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, role-based access control, and audited access logs. We will provide TelemetryOps SOC 2 Type II report on request (attached a summary).

3) Objection process and timeline: Per our DPA, notice triggers a 30-day review window starting 2027-06-27. If Acme raises a reasonable objection within 30 days, well engage to remediate (options include: additional contractual guarantees, operational mitigations such as dataset exclusion, or a targeted IP/data residency constraint). If remediation cannot address the objection within a commercially reasonable period, Acme may exercise the termination right for the affected services.

4) E-sign / execution: Weve provisioned a DocuSign envelope for the addendum: https://app.docusign.com/telemetryops-addendum/ACME-3742. If youre comfortable, sign there and well countersign. If you prefer alternate e-sign (AdobeSign) we can accommodate.

Ive attached a short SCCs summary for quick legal review. Happy to jump on a call to walk through details.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: sccs-summary.pdf (stub)

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acme-energy.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-energy.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: proposed third-party addition (TelemetryOps) + objection window and e-sign

Rishi / Olga —

Thanks for the clarification and the SCC summary. After internal review we have a limited objection: for two telemetry streams that include pseudonymized customer identifiers tied to EU accounts, we need explicit contractual assurance that those datasets will not leave EU infrastructure and that TelemetryOps will only hold keys in the EU.

If Redwood can:
- Add a narrowly tailored clause to the addendum guaranteeing EU-only storage and key management for those datasets, and
- Provide TelemetryOpss SOC2 full report (not just summary) under NDA,

we can waive the objection and sign the addendum via DocuSign. Otherwise we will need the remediation plan and timeline no later than 2027-07-05 so we can decide on the termination right before a planned deployment.

Please escalate as needed and let us know whether Redwood can accept the two bullet points above.

Regards,
Alex Moreno
Head of Security, Acme Energy
